{"id":"COR-929","title":"Grow go-nuts (natsmsg / jsconsumer / backoff) and converge entiredb + entire-api","description":"## Context

<issue id="551acca2-2073-469c-9802-5bb2a2354f67" href="https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-925/extract-shared-entwine-module-connect-drain-jsconsumer-and-converge">COR-925</issue> stood up the shared `go-nuts` NATS module (**v0.2.0**, `github.com/entireio/go-nuts`) and converged **mirror-pipeline** fully onto it — trails #62 (<issue id="09aae455-6ee6-4586-8e51-c9d21cd19dde" href="https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-923/entire-core-nats-shutdown-should-drain-not-close-kills-rollout-noise">COR-923</issue> worker fix) + #63 (all dials → `nuts.Connect`, `internal/natsdial` retired) are both merged. go-nuts currently ships only the connection-lifecycle core: `Connect`, `Drain`, `IsShutdownFetchErr`, `ShutdownGroup`.

This issue tracks the **deferred remainder** — deliberately thin-sliced out of <issue id="551acca2-2073-469c-9802-5bb2a2354f67" href="https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-925/extract-shared-entwine-module-connect-drain-jsconsumer-and-converge">COR-925</issue> so the <issue id="09aae455-6ee6-4586-8e51-c9d21cd19dde" href="https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-923/entire-core-nats-shutdown-should-drain-not-close-kills-rollout-noise">COR-923</issue> deploy-shutdown fix could ship without waiting on the full module. Each package below is a **lift of already-proven prod code**, not new API design.

## 1. Grow go-nuts

- [ ] `go-nuts/natsmsg` — `KeepInProgress` (long-handler AckWait heartbeat, capped so a wedged handler still redelivers) + unified trace-context inject/extract + a `FakeMsg` test double. Lift from entiredb `internal/natsmsg` and entire-api `otelnats` (two impls → one).
- [ ] `go-nuts/jsconsumer` — durable JetStream pull-consumer scaffold (`Start` / `Runner.Stop` / `Process[E]`; AckExplicit, AckWait, bounded MaxDeliver, Term-on-undecodable, span re-parent). Lift from entire-api `internal/jsconsumer`; fold in `IsShutdownFetchErr` + optional `KeepInProgress`. Depends on `natsmsg`.
- [ ] `go-nuts/backoff` — Term-on-final-delivery + flat `NakWithDelay` redelivery policy (the <issue id="3d7afb17-ff11-44dd-8443-80ca438166e8" href="https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-762/meta-fanout-backfill-consumer-orphans-jobs-on-the-work-queue-when-a">COR-762</issue> fix). Lift from mirror-pipeline `fanoutengine`.

**Footprint note:** `natsmsg`/`jsconsumer` pull in the OpenTelemetry API + `nats.go/jetstream` — go-nuts is currently nats.go-only. Conscious dependency decision to make when the first of these lands.

Suggested order: `natsmsg` → `jsconsumer` → `backoff`.

## 2. Converge the remaining services onto `jsconsumer`

- [ ] **entiredb** — Georg's jetstream migration (groups B–D) targets `go-nuts/jsconsumer` instead of a local scaffold; retire entiredb's `internal/natsx` + `natsmsg` in favor of the module.
- [ ] **entire-api** — fold `internal/jsconsumer` + `otelnats` back onto go-nuts (it's the source of both); adopt `nuts.Connect`/`Drain`.

1	// Package natsmsg holds small JetStream message helpers shared by the
2	// hand-rolled pull consumers (permswebhook, repoops).
3	package natsmsg
4	
5	import (
6		"sync"
7		"time"
8	)
9	
10	// keepInProgressMaxTicks caps the total AckWait extension at ~5×AckWait
11	// (ticks fire at AckWait/3). The heartbeat exists so a long handler that IS
12	// making progress — a whole-installation teardown fan-out, a multi-GB
13	// data-plane purge — doesn't get redelivered into a concurrent duplicate;
14	// it must NOT remove the broker's liveness failsafe entirely, or a wedged
15	// handler (hung I/O with no deadline) would pin its delivery to the wedged
16	// replica forever. Past the cap the extension stops and AckWait expiry
17	// redelivers to a healthy replica sharing the durable.
18	const keepInProgressMaxTicks = 15
19	
20	// KeepInProgress calls inProgress at ackWait/3 until stop is called, resetting
21	// the broker's redelivery timer while a long handler runs. The extension is
22	// capped (keepInProgressMaxTicks) — see the constant for why.
23	//
24	// inProgress wraps the message's InProgress call — func() error { return
25	// msg.InProgress() }. The func() error callback keeps this helper decoupled
26	// from the jetstream package.
27	//
28	// A non-positive interval (zero ackWait on a hand-built consumer; New
29	// defaults it everywhere real) returns a no-op stop.
30	//
31	// stop is idempotent and blocks until the ticker goroutine has exited, so
32	// no InProgress can race a terminal disposition (Ack/Nak/Term) issued
33	// after it returns.
34	func KeepInProgress(inProgress func() error, ackWait time.Duration) (stop func()) {
35		interval := ackWait / 3
36		if interval <= 0 {
37			return func() {}
38		}
39		done := make(chan struct{})
40		finished := make(chan struct{})
41		go func() {
42			defer close(finished)
43			ticker := time.NewTicker(interval)
44			defer ticker.Stop()
45			for ticks := 0; ; {
46				select {
47				case <-done:
48					return
49				case <-ticker.C:
50					ticks++
51					if ticks > keepInProgressMaxTicks {
52						return
53					}
54					if err := inProgress(); err != nil {
55						// A delivery that can't be extended (no JetStream
56						// reply subject, or already terminally disposed)
57						// won't start succeeding on a later tick; stop
58						// instead of spinning. The real failure surfaces
59						// on the terminal Ack/Nak/Term.
60						return
61					}
62				}
63			}
64		}()
65		var once sync.Once
66		return func() {
67			once.Do(func() { close(done) })
68			<-finished
69		}
70	}

35	// SubjectToken sanitizes s into a single valid NATS subject token. NATS tokens
36	// cannot contain spaces, dots, or wildcards, so every character outside
37	// [a-z0-9_-] is replaced with '_' (and letters are lowercased). Use it to turn a
38	// human-readable dead-letter reason ("bad completion payload") into a subject

116		msg jetstream.Msg,
117		cfg Config,
118		decode func([]byte) (E, error),

121	) {
122		ctx, span := otelnats.StartConsumerSpan(ctx, otelsetup.Tracer(), msg, cfg.SpanName)
123		defer span.End()
124	
125		ev, err := decode(msg.Data())

130				slog.Any("error", err), slog.String("subject", msg.Subject()))
131			if onUndecodable != nil {
132				onUndecodable(ctx)
133			}
134			_ = msg.Term()
135			return
136		}
137		handle(ctx, span, msg, ev)

## Architecture

**Entire** is a distributed Git repository storage system, split into two planes:

- **Data plane** (`entire-server`) — git smart HTTP, ref CAS, content-addressed object storage, peer-to-peer replication. Backed by PostgreSQL + BadgerDB.
- **Control plane** (`entire-core`) — identity, OAuth/OIDC login, JWKS issuer, SpiceDB-backed authz, repo lifecycle. Backed by CockroachDB + SpiceDB. Modes: `standalone` / `global` / `regional`.

For deeper detail see `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/entire-core/architecture.md`, `docs/glossary.md`, and `docs/adrs/`.

For how this is actually deployed (which clusters/regions run what, per-app overlays, Flux wiring), see the `fleet` repo, cloned as a sibling of this checkout (`../fleet`) — GitOps repo, `clusters/{nonprod,prod}/<cluster>/` are the cluster entrypoints and `apps/<app>/overlays/<cluster>/` are the per-cluster overrides.

For the binaries (`cmd/`), the ports each plane listens on, the top-level package/repo map, and how the components talk to each other (with topology diagram), see **`docs/repo-map.md`** — kept there to keep this file lean.

### Invariants

Load-bearing. Violating them breaks correctness.

- **Content-addressed storage.** Objects in objstore are content-addressed. Hash verification is mandatory before storing received objects.
- **Ref CAS available.** Every refstore implementation exposes `CheckAndSetReference`. Use it for user-driven ref updates so concurrent pushes don't clobber each other. The blind `SetReference` primitive exists for callers that already hold a lock or whose writes are idempotent.
- **DHT keyed by RepoID.** Objects are located by repository ID, not individual object hash. A repo's objects tend to co-locate on the same nodes.
- **Quorum replication.** Writes fan out to the K-closest DHT nodes and block until quorum (≥2 providers succeed across ≥2 distinct AZs — see `checkQuorum` in `objstore/packfile_fanout.go`). Under-replication is tolerated; repair fills it in asynchronously.
- **Consensus-free.** No Raft or Paxos (`docs/adrs/20260320-no-raft.md`). Correctness comes from content-addressing plus PostgreSQL CAS, not consensus.

### Conventions

Current practice. Changeable with an ADR.

1. **Pluggable object storage.** `server/backend/` interfaces allow swapping DISS (DHT + BadgerDB) for PostgreSQL object storage. Refstore is always PostgreSQL.
2. **Two-port server.** Each node runs HTTP (:8080) for clients, Storage gRPC (:8280) for DISS peer-to-peer, separating client traffic from internal replication.
3. **huma/OpenAPI for user-facing APIs, Connect/gRPC for the rest.** User-facing repo (`server/repoapi`) and core (`core/coreapi`) APIs are REST/JSON served via huma at `/api/v1/...` (ADR 20260522-repo-openapi-huma). The `admin` public service still uses Connect (HTTP-compatible gRPC); internal DISS/DHT and core→node services use native gRPC with mutual TLS.
4. **Env vars.** If you must introduce an env var, always name it ENTIRE_.., preferably making it as unambiguous as possible.
5. **Idempotent DDL in CockroachDB migrations.** CRDB does not run in-transaction DDL atomically: a migrator killed mid-run (e.g. a migrate init container preempted by the next rollout) can leave DDL applied with the goose version row unwritten, and the retry then fails on the already-applied statement. Every DDL statement in a CRDB migration (`core/*/migrations/`) must be re-runnable: `CREATE ... IF NOT EXISTS`, `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS`, `DROP ... IF EXISTS`. Concurrent migrators are serialized by a goose table lock (`lockedMigrate` in `cmd/entire-core/cli/migrate.go`), but that doesn't protect against a killed one.

## Coding Philosophy

Write code with the following principles:

### Simple Design (in priority order)

1. Code passes its tests
2. Code reveals intention through clear names
3. No duplication of knowledge
4. Minimal elements—remove anything that doesn't serve the above

### Practices

- Write the test first, or at minimum write it alongside
- Make the change easy, then make the easy change (refactor first when the change is hard; don't bolt the change onto an awkward shape)
- Prefer explicit over clever
- Short methods that do one thing
- Names that make comments unnecessary
- No speculative generality—build what's needed now

### Refactoring

- Leave code cleaner than you found it
- Extract when you see duplication of knowledge, not just code
- Inline when an abstraction isn't earning its keep
- Rename aggressively until the name fits

### Simplicity

- Clear is better than clever
- Start with the straightforward solution; abstract only when patterns repeat
- Inline by default; extract with evidence
- Every abstraction must earn its keep—delete interfaces with one implementation

### Data Orientation

- Prefer plain data structures over custom types when the type adds nothing
- Immutability by default; mutate only when necessary and isolate it
- Derived data beats stored data—don't cache what you can compute
- Separate what from how, and when from what

### Performance Awareness

- Know where allocations happen; avoid them in hot paths
- Prefer sequential memory access over pointer chasing
- Keep hot paths simple and branch-free where possible
- Measure before optimizing, but develop intuition about costs

### Explicitness

- Handle errors at the call site; don't hide them
- Make control flow readable top to bottom
- Small interfaces beat large ones
- A little copying is better than a little dependency

## Interaction Style

- Skip unnecessary acknowledgments.
- Correct me when I'm wrong and explain why.
- Suggest better alternatives if my ideas can be improved.
- Focus on accuracy and efficiency.
- Challenge my assumptions when needed.
- Prioritize quality information and directness.

1	// Package natsx holds small, dependency-light helpers for working with NATS
2	// connections and pull consumers. It intentionally depends only on the standard
3	// library, nats.go, and slogutil so it can be imported by any consumer or serve
4	// package without creating an import cycle back into core.
5	package natsx
6	
7	import (
8		"context"
9		"log/slog"
10		"time"
11	
12		"entire.io/slogutil"
13		"github.com/nats-io/nats.go"
14	)
15	
16	// Drain drains nc and waits (bounded by timeout) for it to flush pending
17	// acks/publishes and reach CLOSED. nats.go's Conn.Drain() is asynchronous — it
18	// starts the drain on a background goroutine and returns immediately — so a
19	// bare Drain() in a shutdown cleanup would let the process exit before the
20	// flush completes. This installs a ClosedHandler to signal completion, starts
21	// the drain, and blocks until the connection closes or timeout elapses. name
22	// labels the connection in the logs so a wedged drain can be attributed.
23	//
24	// The connect-time nats.DrainTimeout option caps only the subscription-drain
25	// phase; nats.go then runs an unconditional ~5s publish flush before closing,
26	// so the true time-to-CLOSED can exceed that option. timeout here is an
27	// independent backstop that bounds how long we block — not a guarantee the
28	// drain finished. Once the consumer loops have joined (COR-923 serve ordering)
29	// there is nothing left to drain, so on a reachable server this returns in
30	// milliseconds; the backstop only bites when the server is unreachable.
31	func Drain(ctx context.Context, name string, nc *nats.Conn, timeout time.Duration) {
32		if nc == nil || nc.IsClosed() {
33			return
34		}
35	
36		closed := make(chan struct{})
37		nc.SetClosedHandler(func(*nats.Conn) { close(closed) })
38	
39		if err := nc.Drain(); err != nil {
40			slogutil.Warn(ctx, "NATS drain failed; closing", slog.String("conn", name), slog.String("error", err.Error()))
41			nc.Close()
42			return
43		}
44	
45		select {
46		case <-closed:
47			slogutil.Info(ctx, "NATS drained", slog.String("conn", name))
48		case <-time.After(timeout):
49			slogutil.Warn(ctx, "NATS drain timed out before close", slog.String("conn", name))
50		}
51	}

1	package natsx
2	
3	import (
4		"context"
5		"errors"
6		"log/slog"
7		"time"
8	
9		"github.com/nats-io/nats.go/jetstream"
10	
11		"entire.io/slogutil"
12	)
13	
14	// Subscriber is the JetStream consumer-management surface a supervised pull
15	// consumer binds. jetstream.JetStream satisfies it; tests substitute a fake.
16	type Subscriber interface {
17		CreateOrUpdateConsumer(ctx context.Context, stream string, cfg jetstream.ConsumerConfig) (jetstream.Consumer, error)
18	}
19	
20	// PullConsumer is the supervise loop shared by every core pull consumer: it
21	// create-or-updates a durable on a stream, consumes from it, and re-creates
22	// after a growing backoff whenever the consume terminates on its own — a deleted
23	// consumer or a closed connection surfaced via ConsumeContext.Closed() — until
24	// ctx is cancelled. The jetstream client owns reconnection and idle-heartbeat
25	// recovery internally; this loop only supervises the terminal cases it surfaces.
26	//
27	// PullConsumer owns the mechanism only. The durable contract (Consumer), the
28	// per-message handling, and each message's ack/nak/term disposition — including
29	// panic recovery, which stays inside the handler where the per-message span
30	// lives — are the caller's Handle. Log lines are composed from Name (e.g.
31	// "email consumer subscribed"); LogFields carries any extra structured context,
32	// such as the op or filter subject that disambiguates sibling consumers.
33	type PullConsumer struct {
34		// Name prefixes every log line, e.g. "email" or "repo-ops".
35		Name string
36		// Subscriber create-or-updates the durable on each (re)connect.
37		Subscriber Subscriber
38		// Stream is the stream the durable binds.
39		Stream string
40		// Consumer is the durable pull-consumer contract. It is re-applied on every
41		// (re)connect, so a drifted tunable reconciles in place.
42		Consumer jetstream.ConsumerConfig
43		// Handle processes one delivery. It owns the disposition (ack/nak/term) and
44		// its own panic recovery, and runs on the nats.go dispatch goroutine.
45		Handle func(ctx context.Context, msg jetstream.Msg)
46		// FetchBatch caps in-flight deliveries (PullMaxMessages).
47		FetchBatch int
48		// RetryBackoff is the initial reconnect backoff; RetryBackoffMax caps it.
49		RetryBackoff    time.Duration
50		RetryBackoffMax time.Duration
51		// LogFields are extra structured attributes appended to every log line.
52		LogFields []slog.Attr
53	}
54	
55	// Run drives the supervise loop until ctx is cancelled.
56	func (p PullConsumer) Run(ctx context.Context) {
57		backoff := p.RetryBackoff
58		for {
59			if ctx.Err() != nil {
60				return
61			}
62			cons, err := p.Subscriber.CreateOrUpdateConsumer(ctx, p.Stream, p.Consumer)
63			if err != nil {
64				// Stream-not-found is expected during a rollout where the consumer
65				// comes up before its stream has been reconciled (or in a dev cluster
66				// without one). Warn rather than Error so on-call isn't paged on
67				// routine startup ordering.
68				if errors.Is(err, jetstream.ErrStreamNotFound) {
69					slogutil.Warn(ctx, p.Name+" stream not yet present, retrying",
70						p.attrs(slog.String("stream", p.Stream), slog.String("durable", p.Consumer.Durable))...)
71				} else {
72					slogutil.Error(ctx, p.Name+" create consumer failed",
73						p.attrs(slog.String("error", err.Error()))...)
74				}
75				if !backoffSleep(ctx, &backoff, p.RetryBackoffMax) {
76					return
77				}
78				continue
79			}
80	
81			cc, err := cons.Consume(
82				func(msg jetstream.Msg) { p.Handle(ctx, msg) },
83				jetstream.PullMaxMessages(p.FetchBatch),
84				jetstream.ConsumeErrHandler(func(_ jetstream.ConsumeContext, cerr error) {
85					slogutil.Warn(ctx, p.Name+" consume error", p.attrs(slog.String("error", cerr.Error()))...)
86				}),
87			)
88			if err != nil {
89				slogutil.Error(ctx, p.Name+" consume start failed", p.attrs(slog.String("error", err.Error()))...)
90				if !backoffSleep(ctx, &backoff, p.RetryBackoffMax) {
91					return
92				}
93				continue
94			}
95			slogutil.Info(ctx, p.Name+" consumer subscribed",
96				p.attrs(slog.String("durable", p.Consumer.Durable), slog.String("stream", p.Stream))...)
97			consumeStart := time.Now()
98			// Capture the completion channel while the subscription is live: Closed()
99			// returns the same channel each call, so capturing once is equivalent to
100			// re-calling it in the select and avoids any post-Stop race.
101			closed := cc.Closed()
102	
103			select {
104			case <-ctx.Done():
105				cc.Stop() // the callback is synchronous; an in-flight handler finishes
106				return
107			case <-closed:
108				// Consume terminated on its own — a deleted consumer or a closed
109				// connection. Recreate after a backoff, resetting it only if the
110				// consume ran healthily for a while first; an immediate close keeps
111				// backing off toward RetryBackoffMax instead of recreating at the init
112				// interval and hammering a recovering server.
113				if time.Since(consumeStart) >= p.RetryBackoffMax {
114					backoff = p.RetryBackoff
115				}
116				if !backoffSleep(ctx, &backoff, p.RetryBackoffMax) {
117					return
118				}
119			}
120		}
121	}
122	
123	// attrs prepends per-call log attributes to the consumer's LogFields.
124	func (p PullConsumer) attrs(head ...slog.Attr) []slog.Attr {
125		return append(head, p.LogFields...)
126	}
127	
128	// backoffSleep waits for the current backoff, then doubles it up to maxBackoff.
129	// Returns false if ctx is cancelled while waiting, so the caller can stop the
130	// run loop.
131	func backoffSleep(ctx context.Context, backoff *time.Duration, maxBackoff time.Duration) bool {
132		select {
133		case <-ctx.Done():
134			return false
135		case <-time.After(*backoff):
136			*backoff = min(*backoff*2, maxBackoff)
137			return true
138		}
139	}

12	// IsShutdownFetchErr reports whether a pull-consumer Fetch error is the benign
13	// result of the connection being drained/closed during shutdown rather than a
14	// real fault. It is only "clean" when ctx is already done — a mid-run
15	// connection loss (ctx still live) is a genuine error worth logging.
16	//
17	// Use it to gate the error log in a fetch loop:
18	//
19	//	msgs, err := sub.Fetch(1, nats.MaxWait(5*time.Second))
20	//	if err != nil {
21	//		if errors.Is(err, nats.ErrTimeout) || nuts.IsShutdownFetchErr(ctx, err) {
22	//			// benign: idle poll, or a drain/close during shutdown
23	//		}
24	//		...
25	//	}
26	func IsShutdownFetchErr(ctx context.Context, err error) bool {
27		return ctx.Err() != nil &&
28			(errors.Is(err, nats.ErrConnectionClosed) || errors.Is(err, nats.ErrConnectionDraining))
29	}
30	
31	// Drain drains nc and waits (bounded by timeout) for it to flush pending
32	// acks/publishes and reach CLOSED. nats.go's Conn.Drain is asynchronous — it
33	// starts the drain on a background goroutine and returns immediately — so a
34	// bare Drain in a shutdown cleanup would let the process exit before the flush
35	// completes. This subscribes to the connection's CLOSED status event, starts
36	// the drain, and blocks until the connection closes or timeout elapses. name
37	// labels the connection in the logs so a wedged drain can be attributed, and
38	// diagnostics are written to logger (defaulting to [slog.Default] when nil).
39	//
40	// timeout is the TOTAL time-to-CLOSED backstop, not the subscription-drain
41	// budget. The connect-time nats.DrainTimeout option caps only the
42	// subscription-drain phase; nats.go then runs an unconditional 5s publish flush
43	// before closing, so the true time-to-CLOSED is up to that flush longer than
44	// nats.DrainTimeout. timeout must exceed the connection's nats.DrainTimeout by
45	// at least the publish-flush budget or it will fire mid-drain and drop pending
46	// acks — [ShutdownGroup] sizes it automatically. timeout bounds how long we
47	// block; it is not a guarantee the drain finished. Once the consumer loops have
48	// joined (see [ShutdownGroup]) there is nothing left to drain, so on a reachable
49	// server this returns in milliseconds; the backstop only bites when the server
50	// is unreachable.
51	//
52	// Unlike a raw nc.Drain, this does not touch the connection's ClosedHandler, so
53	// a handler installed by [Connect] or by the caller (via [WithNATSOptions]) is
54	// preserved, and concurrent Drain calls on the same connection do not clobber
55	// one another.
56	//
57	// Drain is a no-op on a nil or already-closed connection.
58	func Drain(ctx context.Context, nc *nats.Conn, name string, logger *slog.Logger, timeout time.Duration) {
59		if logger == nil {
60			logger = slog.Default()
61		}
62		if nc == nil || nc.IsClosed() {
63			return
64		}
65	
66		// Register for the CLOSED transition before starting the drain so it cannot
67		// be missed, and via a status listener rather than SetClosedHandler so we
68		// never displace a handler the connection already has.
69		closed := nc.StatusChanged(nats.CLOSED)
70		defer nc.RemoveStatusListener(closed)
71	
72		if err := nc.Drain(); err != nil {
73			logger.WarnContext(ctx, "nuts: NATS drain failed; closing",
74				slog.String("conn", name), slog.Any("error", err))
75			nc.Close()
76			return
77		}
78	
79		select {
80		case <-closed:
81			logger.InfoContext(ctx, "nuts: NATS drained", slog.String("conn", name))
82		case <-time.After(timeout):
83			logger.WarnContext(ctx, "nuts: NATS drain timed out before close", slog.String("conn", name))
84		}
85	}

1	// Package jsconsumer is the durable JetStream pull-consumer scaffold shared by
2	// Entire's decode-and-dispatch consumers. Each of those used to hand-roll the
3	// same lifecycle: jetstream.New → CreateOrUpdateConsumer (durable, explicit
4	// ack, bounded ack-wait, bounded MaxDeliver, filter subject) → Consume → stop
5	// on context cancel; and the same per-message prologue: open a consumer span
6	// (re-parented across the NATS hop), decode the payload, and Term on a decode
7	// error.
8	//
9	// This package owns exactly that scaffold and nothing else. Each consumer
10	// keeps its OWN event type, business dispatch, metrics, and log lines — Start
11	// takes the consumer's message callback, and Process invokes the consumer's
12	// handle with the decoded event and the live span. The handler owns the
13	// message's terminal disposition (Ack/Nak/Term); Process never touches a
14	// message that decoded.

16	// Lifted from entire-api's internal/jsconsumer (COR-929), folding in the
17	// module's shutdown classification ([nuts.IsShutdownFetchErr] gates the
18	// consume-error log so a drain during rollout isn't reported as a fault,

25		"fmt"
26		"log/slog"

39	const (
40		// defaultAckWait is how long JetStream waits for an ack before redelivery
41		// when Config.AckWait is zero — comfortably longer than an RPC round-trip
42		// plus a DB upsert, short enough that a stuck message redelivers promptly.
43		defaultAckWait = 30 * time.Second
44		// defaultMaxDeliver caps redelivery before JetStream stops redelivering a
45		// message when Config.MaxDeliver is zero.
46		defaultMaxDeliver = 8
47	)
48	
49	// Config describes the durable consumer to create and how to trace/log it. The
50	// filter is given as either FilterSubject (single) or FilterSubjects (multi),
51	// mirroring jetstream.ConsumerConfig, so a migrated consumer preserves its
52	// existing on-server filter form exactly.
53	type Config struct {
54		Stream         string        // JetStream stream to bind (must already exist)
55		Durable        string        // durable consumer name, stable across restarts
56		FilterSubject  string        // set this OR FilterSubjects
57		FilterSubjects []string      // set this OR FilterSubject
58		AckWait        time.Duration // 0 → defaultAckWait
59		MaxDeliver     int           // 0 → defaultMaxDeliver
60		SpanName       string        // per-message consumer span name (e.g. "repolifecycle.consume")
61		Name           string        // short consumer name, used as the log prefix
62	
63		// Tracer opens the per-message consumer span; nil uses the global OTel
64		// tracer provider.
65		Tracer trace.Tracer
66		// Logger receives the scaffold's own log lines (decode-term warnings,
67		// consume errors); nil uses slog.Default.
68		Logger *slog.Logger
69	
70		// KeepInProgress runs a natsmsg.KeepInProgress heartbeat while handle
71		// executes, for handlers that legitimately outrun AckWait. The extension
72		// is capped, so a wedged handler still redelivers — see
73		// natsmsg.KeepInProgress. The heartbeat stops when handle returns; a tick
74		// racing the handler's own terminal Ack/Nak/Term is a client-side no-op
75		// (nats.go marks the message disposed locally) that halts the heartbeat.
76		KeepInProgress bool
77	}

79	func (c Config) ackWait() time.Duration {
80		if c.AckWait == 0 {
81			return defaultAckWait
82		}
83		return c.AckWait
84	}

87		if c.MaxDeliver == 0 {
88			return defaultMaxDeliver

108	type Runner struct{ cc jetstream.ConsumeContext }

118	// Start creates/updates the durable consumer on nc and begins delivering
119	// messages to onMsg, returning a Runner that Stops when ctx is cancelled. The
120	// stream must already exist (provisioned declaratively); callers whose cells
121	// opt in per-stream gate Start behind that opt-in so a cell without the stream

125	// ([nuts.IsShutdownFetchErr]), which is a clean exit rather than a fault.
126	func Start(ctx context.Context, nc *nats.Conn, cfg Config, onMsg func(jetstream.Msg)) (*Runner, error) {
127		if nc == nil {
128			return nil, fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): nil nats conn", cfg.Name)
129		}
130		js, err := jetstream.New(nc)
131		if err != nil {
132			return nil, fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): jetstream.New: %w", cfg.Name, err)
133		}
134		cons, err := js.CreateOrUpdateConsumer(ctx, cfg.Stream, jetstream.ConsumerConfig{
135			Durable:        cfg.Durable,
136			AckPolicy:      jetstream.AckExplicitPolicy,
137			AckWait:        cfg.ackWait(),
138			MaxDeliver:     cfg.maxDeliver(),
139			FilterSubject:  cfg.FilterSubject,
140			FilterSubjects: cfg.FilterSubjects,
141		})
142		if err != nil {
143			return nil, fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): create consumer %s/%s: %w", cfg.Name, cfg.Stream, cfg.Durable, err)
144		}
145		cc, err := cons.Consume(onMsg, jetstream.ConsumeErrHandler(func(_ jetstream.ConsumeContext, cerr error) {
146			if nuts.IsShutdownFetchErr(ctx, cerr) {
147				return
148			}
149			cfg.logger().WarnContext(ctx, cfg.Name+": consume error", slog.Any("error", cerr))
150		}))
151		if err != nil {
152			return nil, fmt.Errorf("jsconsumer(%s): consume %s: %w", cfg.Name, cfg.Stream, err)
153		}
154		r := &Runner{cc: cc}

163	// consumer span (re-parented to the producer across the NATS hop), decode the
164	// payload, and on a decode error record it, log "<Name>: decode <Stream>;

166	// its own attributes), and Term the message — a poison payload won't decode on

## Subpackages

The root package is deliberately nats.go-only. The consumer-side layers live in
subpackages so importing the root links none of their dependencies (`natsmsg`
and `jsconsumer` add the OpenTelemetry API; all three use `nats.go/jetstream`):

- **`natsmsg`** — small JetStream message helpers: W3C trace-context
  propagation over message headers (`Inject` / `ExtractHeader` /
  `StartConsumerSpan`, so publish → consume stitches into one trace) and
  `KeepInProgress`, an AckWait heartbeat for long handlers, capped so a wedged
  handler still redelivers. `natsmsg/natsmsgtest` ships `FakeMsg`, a scriptable
  `jetstream.Msg` for asserting a consumer's ack/nak/term disposition without a
  broker.
- **`jsconsumer`** — the durable JetStream pull-consumer scaffold:
  `Start` (create-or-update durable → consume → stop on context cancel) and
  `Process` (consumer span re-parented across the NATS hop → decode →
  Term-on-undecodable → dispatch to the handler, which owns the message's
  disposition). AckExplicit, bounded AckWait and MaxDeliver, shutdown-aware
  consume-error logging, optional `KeepInProgress` heartbeat.
- **`backoff`** — the redelivery policy for transiently-failed deliveries: a
  flat `NakWithDelay` envelope bounded by MaxDeliver, with opt-in
  Term-on-final-delivery so a work-queue message is removed cleanly instead of
  orphaning un-acked (COR-762).
